messages:
Olivia CSM: quick sync — AuroraMed onboarding hit intermittent tail latencies on long-context requests (p95 ~720-800ms). onboarding health shows 78% happy, but Jordan flagged UX regressions in the clinical summary flow. Thinking we should try a _latency smoothing_ pilot: soft model swap to a lower-precision variant + a short prefix prefetch cache before changing routing. anyone object?

Ravi Eng: sounds reasonable. can we avoid a hard swap? prefer a canary that routes ~10% traffic to the quantized variant, with soft-fallthrough back to current model for any >1s responses. also add a time-based KV cache for repeated prefixes.

Liam SE: +1. canary + prefix cache is low risk. suggest these defaults: canary 10% -> ramp to 30% if errors <0.5% and p95 improves; rollback immediately if model hallucination rate increases or FNR for key intents goes up.

Maya (CS Ops): Jordan, would that affect any expected outputs for your templates? we need to capture a small eval set for the canary so we can detect quality drift. can you drop 30 representative long prompts (anonymized) in the shared folder?

Jordan (AuroraMed): I can do that by EOD. The UX regressions are mostly around truncated medication lists and occasional formatting oddities. If the quantized model fixes latency but mangles lists, that won't fly. We'll compile examples.

Olivia CSM: plan: 1) ingest Jordan's eval set 2) run offline diff quality check (top-k token overlap + a couple heuristics for lists) 3) launch 10% canary on dedicated pool w/ soft-fallthrough & prefix cache 4) observe 48h then decide ramp/rollback.

Ravi Eng: config snippet I'll push to the canary route (example):
```yaml
route_policy: soft-fallthrough
canary: 0.10
primary_model: rdw-13b-fp16
canary_model: rdw-13b-q4_0
prefix_cache: enabled
cache_ttl: 30s
quality_checks:
  - list_integrity_check
  - intent_fidelity_threshold: 0.98
```

Liam SE: also add token-level sampling logs for the canary so we can surface subtle formatting diffs in the console analytics. leave sampling off for prod to save cost.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started on dedicated-pool-auroramed (canary id: can-20260321-7). routing policy: soft-fallthrough.

Maya (CS Ops): setting up a monitoring page: p95 latency, error rate, list_integrity_score, hallucination alerts, and rollback switch. I'll invite Jordan to view.

Jordan (AuroraMed): thanks — will upload eval set to /shared/auroramed/eval-by-eod. also looping in our PM (Fiona) to watch UX.

Olivia CSM: one more thing — renewal check: customer has renewal in 6 weeks. if canary reduces latency and shows no quality regression, we'll propose the smoothing pilot as part of the renewal value story (predictable UX, lower avg latency). if we see quality drifts, we'll bundle a controlled A/B with fallback routing as an alternative.

Ravi Eng: timeline: quick offline runs today, canary starts now, monitor 48h, then decision. I'll set an auto-rollback at 1.2s p95 or 0.8% error spike.

Liam SE: note: this approach reduces tail latency without changing customer-facing prompts. good pattern for other health-check flagged accounts.

Olivia CSM: perfect. thanks everyone. Jordan — ping here when eval set is uploaded and we'll kick off the offline checks. :thumbsup:
